r.name: Accessible Route, Runnymede
r.description: This is an all-weather, accessible, comfrotable route that runs past Runnymede's key monuments and artworks.

r.name: Views Route, Runnymede
r.description: This route takes you past the Kennedy Memorial, across Cooper's Hill with its view of Windsor Castle and London, then back down past Runnymede's Memorials. This route includes some steps and slopes that can be slippery/muddy.

r.name: Summer Route, Runnymede
r.description: A varied summer route that runs past our key memorials and gives you a sense of the Runnymede landscape, including woods, meadows, ponds and riverside.

r.name: Memorial Route, Runnymede
r.description: This route takes you to all the memorials and artworks at Runnymede, and through the woods to the Commonwealth Airforce Memorial with its lovely views. This route includes some steps and slopes that can be slippery/muddy.

r.name: Egham to Runnymede Countryside Circular Walk, Runnymede
r.description: Wander through woodlands, wetlands & open wildflower meadows home to the birthplace of the Magna Carta. This circular takes you round Runnymede nature reserve, Langham Pond & ancient woodlands, which form a SSSI, for their rare species & the wildflowers

r.name: The Park Circular Walk at Ankerwycke
r.description: Take a leisurely stroll through the park at Ankerwycke on gentle terrain. It's a perfect walk for a lazy Sunday afternoon. Terrain is generally flat, no stiles. Potential livestock in field.

r.name: New Haw Lock to Pyrford Lock Walk, River Wey Navigations
r.description: The River Wey Navigation linked the Thames and a large part of central southern England via the Basingstoke and the Wey and Arun canals. This walk covers parts of the Wey Navigation and the Basingstoke Canal.

r.name: Papercourt Lock to Triggs Lock Walk, River Wey Navigations
r.description: Starting from Papercourt, this walk is based in Send, where the River Wey Navigations has its navigation workshops. On this flat route you'll find locks from the 1760s and ponds and meadows that are important for the local wildlife. Flat & easy walking.

r.name: Wey Navigation Dapdune Wharf to Cartbridge Wharf Walk, River Wey Navigations
r.description: This there-and-back walk takes in some of the most remote parts of the Wey Navigation. Following the towpath along the boundary of Tudor mansion house Sutton Place, it passes former 19th-century corn mill Stoke Mill, several historic locks and two pubs.
